newsitem.title: USA: Intl Lottery sees drop in Q4 revs.
newsitem.headline: Intl Lottery sees drop in Q4 revs.

text.p: International Lottery & Totalizator Sytems Inc said Wednesday it expects fourth quarter revenues to drop below levels seen in last year's fourth quarter and the 1996 third quarter.
The company posted revenues of $5.2 million in the 1995 fourth quarter and $3.5 million in the 1996 third quarter.
The company, which provides computerized ticket processing equipment and services to racing organizations and lotteries, cited its current level of contract orders for the expected revenue decline.
The company said that as of September 30 it had $10 million in working capital, a steady cash position, reduced inventories and no borrowings.

Separately, the company said the San Diego County Superior Court entered a summary judgment on November 1 in favor of International Lottery in a legal action against the company and its president Frederick Brunn by James Walters, the company's former chairman and president.
Walters has filed a notice of appeal with the California appellate court, it said.
